recipes.title: Candied Fruit Loaf Cake
recipes.description: Simple buttery loaf cake to use up leftover candied fruit mix (e.g. Belbake).
recipes.oven: 160°C top & bottom heat, no fan (glass tin)

ingredients.name: baking powder (prášek do pečiva), a bit less than half a packet
extra flour, to coat the fruit

steps.title: Prep
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C, top and bottom heat, no fan. Grease the tin and line it with baking paper.

steps.title: Coat the fruit
steps.text: Toss the candied fruit with 1 tbsp flour so it doesn't sink.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: With the flat beater on medium, beat butter, sugar and vanilla sugar for about 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Add the eggs one at a time on medium speed.

steps.title: Batter
steps.text: Mix flour, baking powder and salt. On the lowest speed, add half the flour, then the milk, then the rest. Stop as soon as it's combined.

steps.title: Fruit
steps.text: Fold in the fruit by hand with a spatula. Spread in the tin.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake on the middle rack. Start checking with a skewer at 35-40 min; usually done at 50-60 min. If the top browns too fast, cover loosely with foil.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool 10 min in the tin, then on a rack. Don't put the hot glass tin on a cold or wet surface.

notes: Lemon or orange zest goes well with it.
Glaze: 4 tbsp powdered sugar + 1 tbsp lemon juice, drizzled over the cooled cake.
No mixer: melt the butter, whisk with sugar, eggs and milk, then stir in the dry ingredients and fruit.

recipes.title: Arsik Kapr (Batak Carp Arsik)
recipes.description: Arsik ikan mas made with Czech carp, simmered in a yellow turmeric and Sichuan-pepper paste with beans and lemongrass. Simplified: no kecombrang or asam cikala.

ingredients.name: carp (kapr), about 1-1.2 kg, cleaned and cut in 4 pieces, or 800 g carp/trout fillets
macadamia nuts (instead of kemiri), for the paste
ground turmeric (kurkuma), or 3 cm fresh, for the paste
galangal (or 1 tsp galangal powder), for the paste
Sichuan pepper, toasted (instead of andaliman), for the paste
red chilies, for the paste (fewer for milder)
green beans (fazolové lusky) or long beans, in 5 cm pieces
lime juice, to finish (instead of asam cikala)

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the fish with lime juice and salt. Leave 15 minutes.

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Toast the Sichuan pepper in a dry pan for 1 minute. Put all paste ingredients in the chopper and blitz to a fairly smooth paste, adding a splash of water if needed.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: In a wide pan, lay the beans and lemongrass on the bottom, then the fish on top. Mix the paste with the water and pour over. Add the lime leaves.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes. Don't stir; spoon the sauce over the fish now and then and gently shake the pan. The sauce should reduce to a thick yellow gravy.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onions and lime juice in the last 5 minutes. Taste for salt. Serve with rice.

notes: Carp has many small bones; trout (pstruh) is easier and cooks in about 20 minutes.
Live and fresh carp are easiest to find in December; frozen carp portions are sold year-round in bigger supermarkets.
Sichuan pepper is a close relative of andaliman and gives the same tingly feeling.

shopping.Sichuan pepper, galangal, lemongrass, li: Sapa market (Praha-Libuš) or Asian grocery shops
shopping.carp, trout, green beans, shallots, maca: regular supermarkets (Albert, Tesco, Kaufland, Billa, Lidl)

recipes.title: Saksang Santan (Pork in Coconut, no blood)
recipes.description: Spicy Batak pork stew with andaliman-style spices, made with coconut milk instead of pork blood. Good in the multi-cooker.
equipment: Lauben multi-cooker 18SB or a pot on the gas stove

ingredients.name: pork shoulder (vepřová plec) or pork belly (bůček), 3 cm cubes
galangal (or 1 tsp powder), for the paste
Sichuan pepper, toasted, for the paste
red chilies (or 1-2 tbsp sambal oelek), for the paste
bay leaves (bobkový list, instead of salam)

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Toast the Sichuan pepper briefly, then blitz all paste ingredients in the chopper.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil, in a pan or using the multi-cooker's frying/sauté program, until lightly coloured.

steps.title: Fry the paste
steps.text: Add the paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and the oil separates a little.

steps.title: Stew
steps.text: Add lemongrass, lime leaves, bay leaves, water, salt and sugar. Pot: cover and simmer on low for about 60 minutes. Multi-cooker: use the stew/slow-cook program; check your manual for the time setting (meat should end up fork-tender).

steps.title: Coconut
steps.text: Add the coconut milk and cook uncovered for 10-15 minutes more, stirring, until the sauce thickens. Taste and adjust salt and chili. Serve with rice.

notes: Traditional saksang uses pork blood; the coconut milk version is a common alternative.
Tastes even better the next day.
Works with chicken thighs too; cut the stewing time to about 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Mie Gomak Goreng (with spaghetti)
recipes.description: Batak fried noodles made with thick spaghetti instead of mie lidi, with a turmeric and Sichuan-pepper paste. Quick weeknight dish.

ingredients.name: Sichuan pepper, toasted, for the paste

steps.title: Pasta
steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until just al dente. Drain and toss with a few drops of oil.

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Blitz the paste ingredients in the chopper.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry the paste in the oil for 3-4 minutes. Add the meat and cook through.

steps.title: Egg and cabbage
steps.text: Push everything aside, scramble the egg in the gap, then add the cabbage and stir-fry for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the spaghetti, kecap manis and soy sauce. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes. Finish with spring onions.

notes: Thick spaghetti (No. 7 or thicker) is the closest to mie lidi.
For mie gomak kuah (soup), add 500 ml chicken stock and 100 ml coconut milk after frying the paste, then add the pasta.

shopping.Sichuan pepper, kecap manis: Asian grocery shops; kecap manis is also in some big supermarkets

recipes.title: Daun Ubi Tumbuk (Greens in Coconut)
recipes.description: Batak pounded cassava leaves in coconut milk. The chopper does the pounding. Uses frozen cassava leaves, or kale/spinach as a substitute.

ingredients.name: frozen cassava leaves, thawed, or 400 g kale (kadeřávek) without stems
Sichuan pepper, toasted, for the paste

steps.title: Chop the leaves
steps.text: Pulse the leaves in the chopper in batches until finely chopped. This replaces pounding.

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Blitz the paste ingredients in the chopper.

steps.title: Cook the leaves
steps.text: Simmer the leaves in the water with the lemongrass. Cassava leaves: at least 20 minutes, until soft. Kale: about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Coconut
steps.text: Add the paste, coconut milk, salt, sugar and anchovies. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until thick.

notes: Cassava leaves must be cooked thoroughly; never eat them raw or undercooked.
Kale gives the closest texture; spinach works but cooks down a lot and is softer.

shopping.frozen cassava leaves: some Asian or African grocery shops (check the freezer section)

recipes.title: Ayam Panggang Andaliman (Oven Chicken)
recipes.description: Simplified ayam napinadar: oven-roasted turmeric chicken thighs tossed in a fresh Sichuan-pepper sambal. No blood sauce.
recipes.time: 15 min prep + 30 min marinate + 40 min roast

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the chicken with turmeric, garlic, lime juice, salt and oil. Leave at least 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast skin side up for 35-40 minutes until golden and the juices run clear. In a glass dish, use 190°C and allow a few extra minutes.

steps.title: Sambal
steps.text: Meanwhile make the Sambal Andaliman.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Toss the hot chicken with half the sambal and serve the rest on the side, with rice.

notes: Traditional napinadar uses a sauce thickened with chicken blood; this version leaves it out.
Can also be pan-grilled on the gas stove: about 8-10 minutes per side on medium heat.

recipes.title: Sambal Andaliman (Sichuan pepper sambal)
recipes.description: Fresh Batak sambal with the tingly citrus kick of andaliman, using Sichuan pepper. Made in the chopper.

ingredients.name: red chilies (or 5 chilies + ½ red bell pepper for milder)

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast the Sichuan pepper in a dry pan for about 1 minute until fragrant. Let it cool.

steps.title: Chop
steps.text: Pulse everything except the lime juice in the chopper to a coarse sambal. Don't make it a smooth purée.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir in the lime juice and salt to taste.

notes: Keeps 3-4 days in a closed jar in the fridge.
Use it with grilled fish, chicken, eggs, or as a side for any of the Batak dishes here.

recipes.title: BPK (Babi Panggang Karo)
recipes.description: Karo-style roast pork, sliced thin and served with a spicy andaliman sauce, rice and greens soup. Simplified: oven or grill pan instead of charcoal, and a blood-free sauce.
recipes.time: 15 min prep + 1 h marinate + 40 min roast
recipes.oven: 220°C top & bottom heat (or fan 200°C), then grill 3-5 min
equipment: wall oven (or grill pan on the gas stove)

ingredients.name: pork neck (krkovice) or pork belly (bůček), slices 2-3 cm thick
garlic cloves, grated, for the marinade
Sichuan pepper, toasted and ground, for the marinade
Sichuan pepper, toasted, for the sauce

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix garlic, ginger, ground Sichuan pepper, black pepper, salt and oil. Rub into the pork. Marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Put the pork on a rack over a tray (add a little water to the tray so the drippings don't burn). Roast 30-40 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and browned.

steps.title: Char
steps.text: Switch to the grill (top heat) for 3-5 minutes to get charred edges. Watch closely. Stovetop option: grill pan on medium-high, 5-7 minutes per side.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Blitz the sauce ingredients (shallots, garlic, Sichuan pepper, chilies, macadamia) in the chopper. Fry in oil for 3-4 minutes, add the tray drippings, water and kecap manis, and simmer 5 minutes until slightly thick. Finish with lime juice and salt to taste.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest the pork 5 minutes, slice thin, and serve with the sauce, Sambal Andaliman, rice and a bowl of greens soup.

notes: Traditional BPK sauce is made with pork blood; this version uses the roasting juices instead.
Krkovice (pork neck) stays juicy and is the easiest cut; bůček gives more fat and crisp edges.
BPK is usually served with a light cassava-leaf soup: make Daun Ubi Tumbuk with extra water and less coconut milk.

recipes.title: Babi Panggang Batak (Toba-style, crispy skin)
recipes.description: Slow-roasted pork belly with crispy skin, the meat side rubbed with a turmeric and andaliman paste. Served with fresh sambal andaliman.
recipes.time: 15 min prep + overnight drying (optional) + 1 h 50 min roast
recipes.oven: 160°C top & bottom heat, then 230°C to crisp the skin

ingredients.name: pork belly with skin (bůček s kůží), one slab
galangal or ginger, for the paste
Sichuan pepper, toasted, for the paste

steps.title: Dry the skin
steps.text: Pat the skin very dry and score it in a fine grid with a sharp knife (cut the skin and fat, not the meat). For the crispiest skin, leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight.

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Blitz the paste ingredients in the chopper. Rub it only on the meat side and edges. Keep the skin clean and dry.

steps.title: Salt the skin
steps.text: Rub 2 tsp salt into the scored skin. Place skin side up on a rack over a tray with a little water in it.

steps.title: Slow roast
steps.text: Roast at 160°C, top and bottom heat, for 1.5 hours.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.text: Brush off excess salt, raise the heat to 230°C (or use the grill) and roast 15-25 minutes until the skin puffs and crackles. Watch closely so it doesn't burn.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 10 minutes, cut into bite-size pieces with a heavy knife, and serve with Sambal Andaliman and rice.

notes: Dry skin is the key to crackling: the drier, the crispier.
If parts of the skin don't puff, put those pieces under the grill for a few minutes.
Ask the butcher for 'bůček s kůží' in one piece; supermarkets often sell it pre-packed.

recipes.title: Babi Goreng Batak
recipes.description: Pork belly first simmered until tender, then fried until golden and crisp, eaten with sambal andaliman and rice. Simple and very forgiving.
recipes.time: 10 min prep + 30 min simmer + 15 min fry
equipment: Lauben multi-cooker 18SB or a pot (for simmering)

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer the pork with water, salt, garlic, ginger and bay leaves for 30 minutes until tender. Multi-cooker: use the stew or soup program; check your manual for the time.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Drain well and pat the pieces dry with kitchen paper. Dry pork fries crisp; wet pork splatters.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Toss with salt, turmeric and ground Sichuan pepper.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan on medium-high. Fry the pork in one layer, turning now and then, for 10-15 minutes until golden and crisp. Use a lid or splatter screen.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with fried shallots and serve with Sambal Andaliman and rice.

notes: Keep the simmering broth: with some greens and andaliman it makes a good soup.
For extra crunch, toss the dried pieces in 2 tbsp cornstarch (kukuřičný škrob / Solamyl) before frying.
